One row per number found in the transcripts, with the reading that was chosen for it. Use the controls to narrow the list, click a column header to sort (click again to reverse), and download what you see as CSV. Hover any control or header for a short explanation.

How to use the controls
Method
Which scoring method's pick to show (compare report: tdt / ctc × segment / word / window; verbalize report: the one method used).
Reference
Compare report only: which hypothesis set the pick is checked against (decides the Outcome).
Outcome
With a reference — success: not flagged and the pick appears in the reference; verify: flagged needs_review; failed: not flagged, a candidate appears in the reference but not the pick (confident and wrong); unchecked: no candidate appears in the reference. Without a reference (verbalize) — accepted: not flagged, written as is; verify: flagged, worth a listen.
Class
Number type in the text: integer, num_suffix (23-ന്), time, ordinal, percent, range, decimal, date, year, phone, …
Form / Language
How the chosen reading is written (contracted, english, ordinal, hh_mm, …) and whether it is Malayalam (ml) or English (en) number words.
Margin ≥ / ≤
Keep numbers whose margin (runner-up score − pick score, nats) is in this range. E.g. ≤ 2 shows the less certain picks.
Search
Words to find (all must match) in the number, candidates, pick, sentence, hypothesis or file name.
Rows per page
Page size; use ◀ Prev / Next ▶ below the table to move between pages.
show every method's pick
Compare report: add a column per method so picks can be compared side by side.
methods disagree
Compare report: only numbers where the methods picked different readings.
pick ≠ default
Only numbers where the audio changed the reading away from the no-audio default.
Reset / Download CSV
Clear all filters and sorting / save the filtered rows (all pages, visible columns) as a CSV.
Counts line
How many numbers pass the filters, and how many of them fall in each outcome (with %).
Colours
The Pick cell is green for success, amber for verify, red for failed.

Malayalam ASR text normalization for WER/CER scoring.

Applied identically to reference AND hypothesis, so scores aren't inflated by
convention/encoding differences. normalize() does: mis-encoded chillu-conjunct fix
(ൻ്റ→ന്റ, NFC-invisible), chillu / ZWJ-ZWNJ canonicalization (indic-nlp-library's normaliser, built
in), Unicode NFC, <unk>('⁇') + punctuation removal, Indic-digit → ASCII,
digit verbalization, English↔Malayalam number canonicalization, lowercase (for
code-mixed English), the CER folds C6 (homoglyph ഠ→0 in a number) and C2 (word-final മ्→ം) in
both modes, plus C1 (word-final samvruthokaram ...ു→...്, eval only), and the opt-in
segmentation fixes W4 (intra-word hyphen join, e-mail→email), W3 (single-letter acronym-run
collapse, എ ടി എം→എടിഎം) and W5 (adjacent-duplicate collapse, വേഗം വേഗം→വേഗം), then whitespace
collapse. All the above are EVAL-mode; inference mode does reader-facing ITN instead (see the
mode selector). See NORMALIZATION.md for the full coverage/gap analysis and the rationale.

Digit verbalization: many ASR tokenizers have NO 0-9 pieces, so a digit left in a
target tokenizes to <unk> and teaches the model to emit '⁇' for spoken numbers. Digits
are expanded to native Malayalam number words ("24" -> "ഇരുപത്തിനാല്", "500" ->
"അഞ്ഞൂറ്"), with standard sandhi joins (glide യ before a vowel-initial part: 21 ->
"ഇരുപത്തിയൊന്ന്"). 1-4 digit runs are read as a number; longer runs and zero-padded
runs (phone/account/OTP-style) are read digit-by-digit ("007" -> "പൂജ്യം പൂജ്യം ഏഴ്").

Number canonicalization (convention-invariant scoring): speakers say numbers in English
or Malayalam, and base models often write English-style numbers in Malayalam script
("ട്വൻറ്റി ഫോർ"). Those are parsed back to a value and re-verbalized through the SAME
Malayalam tables, so "24" / "ട്വൻറ്റി ഫോർ" / "ഇരുപത്തിനാല്" all normalize to the same
form. Ambiguous tokens (ടു = "to", ഫോർ = "for") convert only in a run that also
contains an unambiguous number word.

How it works

Files land in verify/ when a number's reading was uncertain, and in failed/ when verbalize could not process them. In a verify file every confident number is already verbalized; only the uncertain ones are still digits, and only those are shown here — with the sentence audio, the candidate readings (the model's pick ★ pre-selected; Δ = how much less likely than the best, in nats), a box to type your own reading, and later to leave it open. Save applies your readings. When no number is left open the file is written to verbalized/, its rows move from verify.tsv to verbalized.tsv (status verified) and the copy is removed; otherwise it stays in verify/ with the rest.

Spelling: ★ is the pick after the spelling rule — if the audio's own spelling (🔊) beat the others by less than style_margin the default style (contracted) is pre-selected. Choose how each number was spoken by scoring its candidate readings against the audio.

Input: a transcript directory like eval_frozen (one JSON per recording with ``sentences``
[{text, start_time, end_time, ...}] and ``words`` [{word, start_time, end_time}]) and an audio
directory with ``<same stem>.wav``.

For every sentence the text is first normalized with the core normalizer in ``train`` mode
(punctuation stripped except inside numbers), numbers are found with ``digits.find`` and their
readings listed with ``digits.candidates``. Each candidate is then scored with the ASR model:

    unit = "segment"  the whole sentence audio, with that number's candidate substituted and every
                      other number at its default reading (robust to timestamp error, uses context)
    unit = "word"     only the number's own word(s) +- ``context_words`` neighbours, cut out by word
                      timestamps and encoded ON THEIR OWN (no acoustic context outside the window).
    unit = "window"   the WHOLE sentence is encoded once (full acoustic context, shared with the
                      segment unit), then each candidate is scored only on the encoder frames of
                      the number's word window (+- ``context_words`` words, +- ``pad_s``) with the
                      window's text. Accuracy of segment context, cost of a short window.
    "word" and "window" fall back to "segment" for a sentence whose numbers can't be matched
    to timestamped words.

The candidate with the lowest NLL wins. ``margin`` = runner-up NLL - best NLL. ``review_margin`` =
NLL of the best candidate from a DIFFERENT reading family - best NLL, where a family ignores
spelling/word-boundary style (contracted ഇരുപത്തഞ്ച്, glide ഇരുപത്തിയഞ്ച് and spaced ഇരുപത്തി അഞ്ച്
are one family; English, drop-thousand, half, ... are others). Near-ties inside a family are
harmless for the target (all are faithful), so only ``review_margin < margin_threshold`` flags the
number (and its sentence/file) ``needs_review``.

Output: ``<out-root>/<input dir name>/`` (default out-root: ./outputs)

    metrics.html            the same, human-readable report (sortable tables, contents)
    files.tsv               one row per file: duration, counts, durations with digits/SC
    sentences.tsv           one row per sentence: timing, flags, numeric classes, text
    numeric_expressions.tsv every number-bearing word in the set, with its class
    sc_chars.tsv            per-character SC frequency (codepoint, name, class, files)
    digits/<file>.tsv       per file: location of every number-bearing word
    sc/<file>.tsv           per file: location of every special character

Definitions
    digit  any Unicode decimal digit (ASCII 0-9, Malayalam ൦-൯, ...).
    SC     any character that is not a letter, combining mark, digit or whitespace:
           punctuation (P*), symbols (S*: % ₹ × + ...), invisible format chars (Cf: ZWJ,
           ZWNJ, BOM), control/private-use/unassigned. Reported in groups:
             punct    sentence punctuation . , ? ! ; : ' " ( ) and dashes
             symbol   S* categories
             format   Cf (zero-width etc.)
             other    everything else
           and separately as "in a numeric expression" (4:00, 2.5, 70%, 8-9) vs elsewhere.
    numeric expression  a whitespace word containing a digit, classified as date, time,
           time_range, range, decimal, percent, currency, ordinal, phone, id_code, year,
           grouped (1,75,000), slash (6/14), alnum (5G, 10K, ഡി3), num_suffix (23-ന്,
           250യിൽ), integer; anything else is other_numeric.

    is a symmetric scoring fold that can also touch a genuine -u vowel, so it is not applied to
    reader-facing inference output. Together they measurably help WER/CER (dataset WER -1.09).

Example (``examples/digits_scoring.yaml``)::

    model_path: /models/sravaani/v2.nemo   # NeMo hybrid RNN-T(TDT)/CTC checkpoint
    pretrained_name: null               # or a NeMo pretrained name instead of model_path
    cuda: null                          # int = that CUDA device; null = auto; negative = CPU
    allow_mps: true
    compute_dtype: float32              # float32 | bfloat16 | float16 (null = bf16 if available)
    matmul_precision: high              # highest | high | medium
    batch_size: 16                      # (audio, candidate) pairs per forward pass
    tdt_loss: torch                     # torch (pure torch, no numba/libNVVM) | nemo (NeMo's kernel)
    joint_chunk_frames: 16              # encoder frames per joint evaluation (memory bound)
    encoder_batch_s: 30                 # encoder batch budget: clips x longest clip <= this (padded s)
    group_audio_s: 300                  # recordings pooled per scoring group (s of audio; 0 = per file)
    decoding:                           # transcribe() only (compare --transcribe); merged over the
      greedy:                           #   model's own decoding config
        use_cuda_graph_decoder: false   # default false: CUDA graphs crashed after direct scoring
    head: tdt                           # tdt (RNN-T head) | ctc
    unit: segment                       # segment | word (window encoded alone) | window (sentence
                                        #   encoded, number's frames scored)
    pad_s: 0.25                         # audio padding around a segment / word window, seconds
    context_words: 1                    # word unit: neighbouring words included on each side
    max_candidates: 32                  # readings scored per number (first = default); v2: 16 cut 1.3% of numbers, 32 none (+1% scoring)
    style: contracted                   # default native compound style
    margin_threshold: 1.0               # nats; best-vs-best DIFFERENT reading below this -> needs_review
    style_margin: 2.0                   # nats; the audio's spelling (contracted / glide / spaced) is kept
                                        #   only if it beats the other spellings by this; else `style`
    dominant_language_share: 0.8        # a file with more than this share in one language reads every
                                        #   number in it; else per sentence (isolated switches -> review)
    hyp_pad_s: 0.5                      # compare only: hypothesis text within sentence +- this (s)
    length_norm: false                  # compare NLL per token instead of total NLL
    form_costs:                         # nats added to readings the audio over-picks (shorter text
      nosuffix: 6.5                     #   scores lower): written suffix left out
      short_split: 8.0                  #   digit by digit for a number of up to 3 digits (22 -> രണ്ട് രണ്ട്)
      percent: 1.5                      #   പെർസെന്റ് (vs പെർസെന്റേജ്)
      bare_hour: 1.0                    #   11:00 -> പതിനൊന്ന് (vs പതിനൊന്ന് മണി); {} = no costs
    sample_rate: 16000
    out_dir: null                       # verbalize root: OUT_DIR/<data dir>/{verbalized,verify,failed}/<stem>.json + details

indic-normalizer — meaning-preserving text normalization for Indic-script ASR scoring.

The point of this library: when you score ASR with WER/CER you normalize BOTH the
reference and the hypothesis so the metric penalizes real mis-transcriptions, not
encoding/convention differences. The normalization must be *stable* (same input →
same output) and *meaning-preserving* (never collapse a real distinction). See
NORMALIZATION.md for the full design rationale and the Whisper "vanishing vowels"
pitfall this avoids.

Usage
-----
    from indic_normalizer import get_normalizer, normalize

    fn, source = get_normalizer("ml")               # Malayalam, eval mode (default)
    fn("24 രൂപ.")                                    # -> 'ഇരുപത്തിനാല് രൂപ'

    fn, _ = get_normalizer("ml", mode="inference")  # reader-facing ITN
    fn("ഇരുപത്തിനാല് രൂപ")                            # -> '24 രൂപ'

    normalize("ഇ–മെയിൽ", lang="ml")                  # one-shot, eval
    normalize("24 രൂപ.", lang="ml", mode="inference")# one-shot, ITN -> '24 രൂപ.'
    normalize("ഇരുപത്തിനാല്!", lang="ml", mode="inference", itn=False)  # -> 'ഇരുപത്തിനാല്!'
    normalize("hello, world")                        # no lang -> universal normalizer

`get_normalizer(lang, mode)` returns ``(normalize_fn, source_label)``. A language with a
dedicated normalizer (e.g. Malayalam) uses it; everything else falls back to the
language-agnostic ``universal`` normalizer. ``mode`` is "eval" (default; WER/CER
scoring — numbers verbalized to native words), "train" (aliases "training", "fine-tune"; same but numbers
left as written) or "inference" (reader-facing ITN: number words -> digits, punctuation + case
preserved; ``itn=False`` keeps number words as written). See NORMALIZATION.md "Mode selector".

Adding a language: drop ``languages/<lang>.py`` (exposing ``normalize(text, mode)``) and
register its aliases in ``registry._ALIASES`` + a branch in ``registry._load``.

indic_normalizer.digits — digit normalization (numbers -> spoken words), separate from core.

Core (``indic_normalizer.normalize`` / ``get_normalizer``) is untouched by this module. Use it
to turn numbers in TRAINING TARGETS into the words that were actually spoken, so the targets
contain no digits or number punctuation (4:00-5:00, 2.5, 70%, 23-ന്).

    from indic_normalizer import digits

    digits.verbalize("ഫീസ് 1,75,000 ആണ്, 4:00-5:00 വരെ")
    # -> 'ഫീസ് ഒരു ലക്ഷത്തി എഴുപത്തയ്യായിരം ആണ്, നാല് മണി അഞ്ച് മണി വരെ'

    digits.find(text)          # [NumberSpan(core='1,75,000', cls='grouped', token_index=1, ...), ...]
    digits.candidates("25")    # [ഇരുപത്തഞ്ച് (ml, contracted), ഇരുപത്തിയഞ്ച് (ml, glide), ട്വന്റി ഫൈവ് (en)]

Choosing the reading
--------------------
A digit does not say HOW it was spoken: in the eval calls ~40% of numbers are said in English
(ഫോർ, തൗസന്റ്, ലാക്ക്), halves as രണ്ടര, times as നാലര / ആറേമുക്കാൽ. ``candidates()`` lists
the plausible readings (native contracted, native glide, English, plus class-specific forms);
``verbalize(text, chooser=...)`` calls your chooser for every number so the pick can come
from the audio — e.g. score each candidate with an ASR model (RNN-T / CTC log-likelihood of
the candidate text on that word's audio window, located via ``span.token_index`` in a
word-timestamped transcript) and return the best. Without a chooser the first candidate
(native, ``style``) is used.

The Malayalam forms are in ``indic_normalizer.digits.ml``; other languages can be added as
sibling modules.
